title: Check if There is a Path With Equal Number of 0's And 1's
summary: Given a binary matrix, determine if there exists a path from the top-left to the bottom-right corner that contains an equal number of 0s and 1s.
statement: Given a binary matrix, determine if there exists a path from the top-left to the bottom-right corner that contains an equal number of 0s and 1s. You can only move right or down.
constraints: grid is a nonempty rectangular binary matrix.
Move only right or down from the top-left through the bottom-right cell.
Return whether some path visits equal counts of zeros and ones.
hints: All paths to a cell share the same length but may contain different counts of ones.
Store the reachable one-counts at every cell from its top and left predecessors.
Reject odd total path length; otherwise test whether half the length is reachable at the destination.
The transition enumerates every right/down predecessor and adds the current bit, so the destination set contains exactly all possible one-counts.
editorial: The transition enumerates every right/down predecessor and adds the current bit, so the destination set contains exactly all possible one-counts.

tests.explanation: A six-cell route exists with three zeros and three ones.
Every five-cell path has odd length, so equal counts are impossible.
